preserves_historical_record.summary: The historical record proves a 228-path derivation with a documentation-only positive control (9e2dddc -> 3323fcb) and a single compiled-.cpp negative control (3323fcb -> 69d1b61 naming tests/engine/bench_first_generation_publish.cpp). It predates the header-closure coverage fix and contains no header-only, unresolved-include, or CMake negative row. Its path count and control set remain identifiable as historical and are NOT the current validation.
preserves_historical_record.current_note: This v2 record is the current validation. The historical 228-path row is not edited into agreement with the numbers below (382 paths); they are different derivations at different times.

synthetic_commit_isolation.cleanup_policy: The temporary worktree and branch are removed before the final push; only the feature branch is pushed. A reviewer can recreate each control from the exact mutations recorded below.

gate_defects_found_and_fixed_by_this_val.severity: high (silent closure truncation — false coverage completeness)
gate_defects_found_and_fixed_by_this_val.what: Get-BlobText returned a per-line string array; [regex]::Matches coerces a string[] argument by joining with spaces, destroying the (?m)^ line anchors. The include closure therefore matched at most one include per file (a file's very first line) and silently excluded every nested header.
gate_defects_found_and_fixed_by_this_val.how_caught: Control 6 (nested-header mutation of src/protocol/include/ffprotocol/WindowsPath.h) initially reported PASS with identical digests; a debug run proved 0 include matches for non-first lines.
gate_defects_found_and_fixed_by_this_val.fix: Get-BlobText returns the blob as one raw string.
gate_defects_found_and_fixed_by_this_val.post_fix: Derived coverage rose 241 -> 382 executable-impacting paths; the nested-header control now FAILs and names WindowsPath.h.

gate_defects_found_and_fixed_by_this_val.what: Resolve-Include returned 'GENERATED:<build path>' for ANY include name that matched a build-tree include root without checking that the artifact exists, so an unresolved quoted project include (e.g. ff_apply_control_missing_header.h) hid behind the build-output escape and the gate reported coverage proven.
gate_defects_found_and_fixed_by_this_val.how_caught: Control 4 (unresolved quoted include in src/engine/src/IndexPipeline.cpp) reported PASS even after the closure fix; a debug run showed resolution to 'GENERATED:build/release-test/generated/ff_apply_control_missing_header.h' for a file that does not exist.
gate_defects_found_and_fixed_by_this_val.fix: A GENERATED verdict now requires the candidate to exist on disk as a leaf file; nonexistent candidates fall through to the fail-closed path.
gate_defects_found_and_fixed_by_this_val.post_fix: Control 4 now FAILs closed with 'unresolved-quoted-include: src/engine/src/IndexPipeline.cpp -> ff_apply_control_missing_header.h'.

gate_defects_found_and_fixed_by_this_val.what: MSVC emits include roots containing '..' segments (e.g. 'D:\...\tests\ui\..'); the derivation stored them un-canonicalised ('tests/ui/..'), which never matched normalised tracked paths, so includes resolved by those roots (tests/TestSupport.h) appeared unresolved.
gate_defects_found_and_fixed_by_this_val.how_caught: After the fail-closed fix, the positive control itself FAILed listing 'tests/ui/test_home_interaction.cpp -> TestSupport.h'.
gate_defects_found_and_fixed_by_this_val.fix: Include roots are canonicalised with GetFullPath before normalisation to repository-relative form.
gate_defects_found_and_fixed_by_this_val.post_fix: TestSupport.h resolves; the positive control passes again.

gate_defects_found_and_fixed_by_this_val.what: Resolve-Include resolved a quoted include against the including file's own directory only when the name began with './' or '../', but MSVC searches the includer's directory for EVERY quoted name ('#include "WindowsPath.h"' inside ffprotocol/). Bare quoted names were checked only against include roots and the repository root.
gate_defects_found_and_fixed_by_this_val.how_caught: Control 6's initial PASS showed WindowsPath.h (included by SnapshotFormat.h from its own directory) outside the derived set.
gate_defects_found_and_fixed_by_this_val.fix: Quoted includes now resolve against the including file's directory first, exactly like the compiler; angle includes skip that step.
gate_defects_found_and_fixed_by_this_val.post_fix: WindowsPath.h enters the closure and its mutation moves the digest.

coverage_boundary_recorded_not_failed.note: Unresolved quoted includes from third_party/ amalgamation sources are recorded as coverageNotes, not coverage failures: the vendored SQLite amalgamation carries platform-conditional quoted includes (mingw.h, _mingw.h, sqlite_cfg.h, windows.h, tclsqlite.h, sqlite3rtree.h) naming toolchains outside this repository that are not compiled here. Every quoted include in project source (src/, tests/, verify/, cmake/) still fails closed when unresolved. This exception is directory-scoped, recorded in every gate output, and does not affect the digest claim.

claim_boundary_design_D4.proves: Git-controlled executable-impacting source and build-input equivalence between two revisions: the derived translation-unit set from build/release-test/compile_commands.json, the recursive quoted/angle include closure over the recorded include roots, and executable-affecting CMake/version build inputs, digested as <path>\0<git blob id>.
does_not_prove: compiler command-line flags not modelled by the digest
claim_boundary_design_D4.compile_command_hashing_decision: DEFERRED, not rejected (task 3.4): none of the seven controls demonstrated a command-line-only difference that this campaign's certification relationship would falsely certify, so compile_commands.json command lines are not hashed. Add that only if such a control appears. A full reproducible-build project is out of scope.

conclusion: All seven controls produced their expected verdicts against the repaired gate. A passing gate run now demonstrates a relationship capable of failing in all five mandated ways; the historical 228-path record remains preserved as historical evidence.
